query_text: where does the sound come from when you crack your knuckles

content.text:
The “crack” sound from cracking your knuckles mostly comes from **gas bubbles rapidly forming inside the joint fluid**.

Your knuckle joints contain **synovial fluid**, a slippery fluid that lubricates the joint. When you pull or bend a finger to crack it, you briefly **increase the space inside the joint**, which lowers the pressure. Dissolved gases in the fluid — mainly carbon dioxide — can suddenly come out of solution and form a bubble or cavity. That rapid formation is called **cavitation**, and it creates the popping sound.

A couple related points:

- After cracking, the joint usually can’t crack again right away because it takes time for the gases to dissolve back into the fluid.
- The sound usually does **not** mean bones are grinding together.
- Habitual knuckle cracking has not been strongly shown to cause arthritis, though forceful or painful cracking is a reason to stop or ask a clinician.
